about: S3's river as the builder builds it (blender/rainbow_bridge_scene.py), written by the river agent (S3 Run 2, scratchpad S3_run2_river/plan.py, write_plan.py). Metres, X east, D north (the world frame). water: per water map ID the shore lines handed to kb.water_strip as the entity's lines (H stays the frame's water H, -0.7), west to east, the two reaches meeting exactly on the scan line u 18300. banks: continuous lines for the ground's heightfield, the ground falling from top (H 0) to shore (water H). far_bank: the strip of land west of the bridge's north foot. edges: the land parts of the seam walls. far_bank_move: the recorded move of the far bank (choices/river.json moves list every entity that moves with it).

S3.water.bian_west_15500.why: West seam: both shores start exactly on S4b's (u 15500): the near shore at S4b's mapped near-shore end (88.39, 14.11), the far shore at S4b's moved far-shore end (82.12, 29.40) + (-2.26, +5.5) = (79.86, 34.90) (S4b.water.bian_river, moved 5.5 m north along the receding direction; build_rules lead's note), so the strip's west closing runs along the seam line itself (both ends lie on u 15500) and meets S4b's water edge to edge. Near shore: as mapped (est behind the riverside hall, the reeds and the shed) to the land at the bridge's south-west foot, then 0.6 m off the south ramp's far skirt to the south abutment (river_e: the painted water meets the deck's west edge at u 18300-18480; the mapped shore there was a placeholder under the deck). Far shore: the far bank's mapped tops (its est shores lie 0.5-1.1 m north of them: the lead's call, water only to the bank tops), moved north with the far bank (far_bank_move), joined to S4b's moved shore at the seam across the far bank's run-off past the silk's top edge (S3.grd.far_bank_seam_15500, moved with it). At u 18300 (the far-bank shed moved, the hall on stilts not) the far shore steps back south along u 18300 itself to the hall on stilts' bank top (117.40, 25.85), unmoved, where the east reach begins.

S3.water.bian_river_18300.why: Starts on u 18300 where the west reach ends. Near shore: 0.6 m off the south ramp's far skirt, then the south abutment's river face (bridge_plan.json abutments[0], s 5.36: the mapped est shore crossed the deck at s 3.5-4.9 and the abutment straddled it; with the face as the shore the arch springs from the water's edge and the ramp's far side stands at the water, as painted), then the mapped south-bank shores to the S2 seam (156.16, 7.49), S2's first point. Far shore: the far-bank hall's mapped shore (south of its tops), the mapped shore under the bridge's far half to the arch's far edge, then the arch's far edge and the north abutment's river face (s 20.17; the bridge agent's proposal: the mapped shore ran diagonally under the arch, leaving up to 5.4 m of north bank under its far half where the soffit is 0-2.6 m above the ground), then the north bank's mapped tops east of the bridge, 0.4 m out (its est shore lies up to 0.86 m north of them), to the S2 seam at S2.grd.north_bank_20500's first bank top (149.37, 24.68).

far_bank.why: Closed. (1) It is painted at 0.22-0.35 of the street's scale: its real-size shops fill its 1.5-4.7 m strip to the silk's top edge, with no room to walk in front of them. (2) It is moved 5.5 m north (west of u 18300; the hall on stilts and the bridge stay) to make room for the boats at real size, as S4b's was, which puts it at and past the silk's top edge, in the mist. (3) It has no painted way to the walkable area: under the arch the water now reaches the north abutment's face, and round the north ramp's west side the way lies beyond the silk's top edge (D > 30.5). (4) S4b's far bank is closed, so a walkable strip would dead-end at the seam. Closed by the water itself (the near shore's edge:shore walls), the bridge's railings and ramp skirts, and the north edge wall; no wall of its own.

edges.why: The land parts of the seam walls: the S4b seam from the painted area's sw corner to the near shore; the S2 seam from the se corner to the south shore and from the north shore to the ne corner. The water between them has no seam wall: boats cross both seams (S4b's sterns into S3, S3's big boat and the moored south-bank boat into S2), and the shore walls close the water.

far_bank_move.about: dD (m north) by scan u; each far-bank point moves dD along the receding direction at its own u (dX = -dx(u)/77 * dD), so it keeps its place along the scroll. 5.5 m from the S4b seam (S4b's own move) to u 18300, then 0: the far bank's buildings stand at its bank top end to end, so a taper would leave a building's corner in the water; the step falls between the far-bank shed (moved) and the hall on stilts (not moved), along the scan line u 18300 itself (the two reaches' seam), so the hall on stilts stands on a short promontory with water on its west side. Every moved entity is in choices/river.json moves.
